correctness.rationale: Matrix B=W+E00 has characteristic polynomial (z+1)p_{n-1}; the polynomial identity p_{n-1}=z^(2^s-1) p_{m-1}^(2^s) for n=2^s m, m odd, proves exact zero algebraic multiplicity q=2^s-1. Solving Bx=0 gives nullity exactly one at even lengths and zero at odd, hence precisely one nilpotent Jordan block of size q. Fitting decomposition proves shell counts for every n and t. Uniform comparison follows by the Laurent-polynomial model. Actual verifier at verify.py confirms matrix-power rank profiles for n=3..80, full first-repeat enumeration for n=3..11, and direct characteristic polynomials for n=3..17. Finite checks corroborate but do not replace proof.

originality.rationale: The assessed statement treats a finite cyclic binary Rule 90 system with exactly one site changed to Rule 150, and derives its complete first-periodic-entry law. Uniform Rule 90 literature supplies a determinant identity but does not state the defect-specific Jordan or shell populations. General non-uniform literature uses different scopes. No inspected source implies this entire claim; one plausible inaccessible paper remains a qualified risk.

value.rationale: Single-rule cellular defects are a natural test of the robustness of finite symbolic dynamics. This perturbation has a sharply quantified structural consequence: it removes the odd-ring singularity and merges two even-ring nilpotent blocks into one longer chain, simultaneously doubling periodic density and changing the entire first-periodic-entry law. Exact dyadic horizon and shell populations are meaningful natural dynamical invariants for every ring size, not an arbitrary finite sample.
